answer.rationale: Finance mandates 18% spend cut; contract expires in 14 days with no auto-renew; line at 94% volume, no buffer. Renewing incumbent preserves integration stability across cycles, no migration work, no delivery interruption. Multi-year commitments with incumbent unlocked volume pricing per memory_c6. Cutting unit cost without narrowing service scope. Given the tight 14-day deadline and zero buffer, switching or adding sources carries delivery risk. Deferring sacrifices the mandated cut. Renegotiating terms may not achieve 18% cut in 14 days. Renew incumbent is the only direction that meets all three constraints: cost, risk, timeline.
